Hi Alice / Bob,

Thanks again for taking the time today - great conversation. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so your legal team has everything in one place:

- Use case: Orion will send user-generated analytics queries to Redwood to power the "Query Assist" feature. Some queries may contain PII (email, phone, device identifiers).
- Primary asks from Orion: data residency (US-only), retention windows for logs/KV cache, processor/subprocessor disclosures, and breach notification timing.

Attached is our latest DPA (Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf) - it reflects our standard terms for hosted API contracts. A few specific points to call out so we can accelerate:

1) Roles: Redwood operates as a processor; Orion will be the controller.
2) Subprocessors: Redwood maintains a subprocessors list and provides notice before adding new subprocessors. We can provide a current list and a URL that customers can reference.
3) Breach notification: our standard is "without undue delay" and we aim to provide detailed initial notification within 72 hours for confirmed incidents that affect customer data.
4) Data residency: hosted API is multi-region by default; for US-only residency we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private. We can provide a written commitment for regionally pinned deployments under Dedicated/Private engagements.
5) Retention: default logs/trace retention is 30 days; KV cache and model context may be kept per workload. We can agree on shorter retention or auto-purge options for regulated customers.

Can you confirm the priority items for your legal team? If helpful, I'm happy to set up a short triage call with our privacy/infosec folks (Dev - cc'd) to walk through specifics.

Next steps I propose:
- You send any DPA redlines/questions (if you have them)
- We review and either provide redline responses or schedule a legal sync (depending on complexity)

Thanks - talk soon.

Best,

Hi Alice - thanks for the redlines and the clear asks. I checked with our privacy and product teams this morning; summarized answers below (we've also attached a short Q&A doc with inline responses):

1) Roles
- Confirmed: Orion = Controller; Redwood = Processor. We'll sign the DPA as processor.

2) Subprocessors
- Current subprocessors list: we will provide a complete list via a customer-facing URL and include a snapshot in the DPA response. We notify customers via email at least 30 days prior to adding a new subprocessors where feasible. For critical security patches or vendor changes that require immediate action, we will notify as soon as practicable.

3) Breach notification
- We can commit to providing an initial notification "without undue delay" and will aim to provide confirmed initial notification within 72 hours for incidents that materially impact customer data. Follow-up communications will include scope, mitigations, and remediation plans.

4) Data residency
- Hosted (multi-tenant) API does not provide contractual US-only isolation by default. US-only residency is available via Redwood Dedicated or Private (we can provide a written commitment in the DPA for region-pinned deployments for dedicated/private customers). Estimated uplift: typical Dedicated engagements start at a 6-8 week lead time and have a pricing uplift depending on capacity and SLA; I can provide a ballpark after we scope expected throughput.

5) Retention and purge controls
- Default logs / request traces: 30-day retention. We support contractually enforced retention and can offer configurable purge windows down to 7 days for logs/telemetry. KV cache and model context retention are workload-dependent; for PII-sensitive workloads we recommend session-less or ephemeral context and can include contractual language to restrict retention.

6) SOC 2 / compliance
- I'll share a link to our compliance portal (or provide an SOC 2 in-scope statement) as part of the legal pack.

Next steps:

- If you'd prefer a legal-to-legal call, I'm happy to schedule a 30-min sync with Neha and Dev.
